items.headline: Haaland sale hinges on captaincy confidence before Arsenal trip
items.summary:
Erling Haaland’s away match against Arsenal in Gameweek 12 revives the case for selling Manchester City’s premium forward and redistributing his funds, particularly with several expensive alternatives entering stronger fixture runs. A month ago, that route looked far less appealing because Manchester United and Alexander Isak had unreliable form and difficult schedules, but the landscape has shifted enough to make the debate credible.

The key obstacle is captaincy. Selling Haaland only becomes attractive if managers trust other premium options with the armband on a regular basis. João Pedro, Cole Palmer, Bruno Fernandes and Alexander Isak are cited as possible captaincy alternatives, but there is not yet enough confidence in them to make Haaland expendable. Keeping him preserves a dependable captaincy option even when Manchester City face tougher opposition.

The immediate fixture case for a sale is clear: Haaland visits Arsenal, while Bruno Fernandes has Brentford at home and both Isak and Chelsea have favourable upcoming matches against Crystal Palace and Nottingham Forest. Moving Haaland on also frees enough money to strengthen elsewhere, including upgrading defence to Arsenal’s Gabriel. The potential gain is a more balanced squad with several high-upside assets rather than one dominant premium.

However, the recommendation remains cautious. Haaland will still score goals, and managers who sell him need the temperament to absorb potential hauls without immediately trying to reverse the move. The strategy requires commitment because rebuilding to bring him back can be difficult. A Free Hit can offer a temporary route back to Haaland in an especially attractive captaincy week, but there are currently no major plans to sell him outright.
key_points: Haaland’s Gameweek 12 away fixture at Arsenal makes a sale and funds redistribution a viable discussion.
Captaincy is the deciding factor: sell only if João Pedro, Cole Palmer, Bruno Fernandes or Alexander Isak feel reliable enough to captain regularly.
Bruno Fernandes faces Brentford at home, while Isak and Chelsea have favourable fixtures against Crystal Palace and Nottingham Forest.
Selling Haaland could finance upgrades such as Arsenal defender Gabriel while improving the overall squad balance.
A Free Hit can provide short-term access to Haaland for a standout captaincy fixture without permanently owning him.
Managers who sell Haaland need to tolerate the risk of his returns, as buying him back quickly may be difficult.

items.title: FPL GW12: Transfer Plans - Raya OUT! ❌ 2x Transfers Used
items.headline: Raya injury pushes Palmer-to-Bruno Fernandes switch ahead of Gameweek 12
items.summary:
Gameweek 11 is a low-scoring anomaly rather than a cue for wholesale changes. Popular captaincy options all fail: Erling Haaland blanks, Nicolas Jackson offers no better return and the alternative captaincy choices disappoint. Double-ups on Arsenal and Brighton defence also hurt as both sides concede, but their underlying season-long defensive value remains intact. Brighton’s 2-0 defeat at Hull is especially misleading: they dominate the chance data, generate 2.24 xG and only collapse after Costa’s late red card, with Oli McBurnie scoring twice after the 92nd minute. Brighton assets remain holds rather than panic sales.

The major immediate concern is David Raya, who goes off with a shoulder problem against Newcastle. Early assessment suggests anything from a two-to-six-week absence, with even the optimistic scenario likely to cover three gameweeks because of the midweek schedule. Managers with only one active goalkeeper should plan to sell, while those with a playing deputy can wait for firmer news. Kinsky is the preferred cheaper replacement in the proposed plan, although Trafford is also considered.

The key midfield decision is whether to retain Cole Palmer. Palmer’s recent underlying numbers are described as alarming: he records little goal threat or creativity, has not scored a non-penalty goal since Gameweek 2 and his few recent assists are viewed as fortunate rather than evidence of sustained output. Selling Raya for Kinsky and Palmer for Bruno Fernandes is favoured over a Raya-to-Trafford move combined with bringing in Calvert-Lewin, because the latter route forces Palmer to stay and creates an unconvincing Leeds triple-up.

Fernandes is a short-term, fixtures-driven punt rather than a long-term value pick. Manchester United’s defence remains highly targetable after another error-strewn display against Liverpool, but their attack still carries quality and Fernandes continues to shoot, create and take penalties. Brentford in Gameweek 12, followed by Coventry and Crystal Palace after a planned Gameweek 13 Free Hit, gives him captaincy potential; he is the leading armband option for Gameweek 12, with Mafeovich a riskier alternative. Haaland is not the intended captain. The wider strategy is to Free Hit in Gameweek 13, then reassess Chelsea assets and potential moves such as Jackson to Joao Pedro once fixtures and minutes improve.
key_points: Do not sell Brighton assets after the Hull defeat: Brighton dominate the match on xG and lose their clean sheet only through a late ten-man collapse.
David Raya is a likely Gameweek 12 sell for managers without a second playing goalkeeper, with his shoulder issue potentially ruling him out for at least three gameweeks.
Kinsky is the preferred Raya replacement, while Trafford is an alternative that can facilitate a move for Calvert-Lewin.
Cole Palmer is a sell candidate after persistently poor non-penalty xG and xA numbers, despite his penalty-taking role.
Bruno Fernandes is the preferred Palmer replacement as a short-term Manchester United attack punt and a Gameweek 12 captain option against Brentford.
Manchester United defenders remain avoidable, but their attackers are worth considering for upcoming fixtures against Brentford, Coventry and Crystal Palace.
A Gameweek 13 Free Hit remains the planned chip strategy, allowing aggressive short-term transfers before resetting the squad.
Monitor price changes closely: Kinsky is close to a rise and Raya and Palmer may fall, making an early goalkeeper move plausible.

items.title: 🚨 Raya INJURED 🚨 FPL Kneejerk Gameweek 12 🔥
items.headline: Bruno Fernandes emerges as the Gameweek 12 captaincy punt despite Manchester United doubts
items.summary:
Gameweek 11 is a low-scoring round for many managers, with 35 points looking disappointing but not disastrous amid widespread blanks. The immediate focus is on avoiding reactionary early transfers before European fixtures, particularly after Manchester United’s heavy defeat at Liverpool. That result is tempered by an early red card for Leny Yoro, and Bruno Fernandes remains a viable short-term target because Manchester United host Brentford in Gameweek 12 and face Coventry in Gameweek 14. Bruno is the preferred captain if bought this week, although waiting until Gameweek 14 is a reasonable alternative for managers unconvinced by United.

Cole Palmer is the key transfer dilemma. His recent form is poor, but Chelsea’s run of Aston Villa at home, Coventry away, Newcastle at home, Crystal Palace away and Sunderland at home makes him difficult to sell. The only compelling immediate switch is Palmer to Bruno; otherwise, Palmer is worth holding rather than moving to a Liverpool midfielder. Morgan Gibbs-White is also a hold, with Chelsea at home followed by Hull, while Bryan Mbeumo remains a hold despite some concern over his early substitution and future minutes.

A Raya injury could reshape goalkeeper plans, but the severity is still unknown. If Raya is absent long term, Alisson is an appealing one-transfer replacement due to Liverpool’s extended fixture run, albeit with his own injury risk. James Trafford is attractive for strong home fixtures and save-point potential, while Bournemouth’s Djordje Petrovic offers value at £4.5m. Trafford and Guglielmo Vicario/Kinsky-style rotation is tempting in the short term, but using multiple transfers on goalkeepers is less appealing than simply buying Alisson. Arsenal’s reserve goalkeeper is only a short-term solution if Raya’s absence is brief.

Liverpool assets are increasingly attractive: Florian Wirtz is in excellent form and Liverpool’s fixtures are strong, while Alexander Isak and Dominik Szoboszlai are also among the leading attacking options. Wirtz is preferred to Bournemouth’s Marcus Tavernier where the latter’s four-yellow-card suspension risk is a deciding factor. A Liverpool-heavy route, potentially adding Alisson, Wirtz and a defender such as Jarell Quansah or Virgil van Dijk, points towards Free Hit 14, when Liverpool visit Chelsea. There is no perfect Free Hit week, however; Gameweeks 12 to 19 can all work depending on squad structure, with Gameweek 19 offering Arsenal versus Ipswich and Liverpool versus Coventry.

Erling Haaland at Arsenal is benchable if a manager has 11 stronger options, but there is no need to force him out. He should not be captained in Gameweek 12, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Brighton’s Diego Gomez/Kadewere-style options and Bruno among alternatives discussed. Calvert-Lewin is preferred to Leeds alternatives such as Mirovic for the armband, while Mirovic is a strong defensive transfer target but less urgent for managers planning to Free Hit in Gameweek 14. The standout tongue-in-cheek recommendation is Brentford’s Sharda as captain against Manchester United, but the serious captaincy preference is Bruno if owned, otherwise Calvert-Lewin or another high-minutes attacker with a favourable fixture.
key_points: Do not make an early Gameweek 12 transfer before European fixtures and further news on Raya’s injury.
Bruno Fernandes is the preferred premium transfer and captain against Brentford, but waiting to buy him for Gameweek 14 is viable.
Keep Cole Palmer unless selling him directly funds Bruno Fernandes; Chelsea’s fixtures remain strong despite Palmer’s poor form.
If Raya is out long term, Alisson is the simplest replacement, while Trafford offers save-point upside and Petrovic preserves funds.
Florian Wirtz is the leading Liverpool midfield target; his form and fixtures outweigh Tavernier’s appeal given Tavernier is on four yellow cards.
Free Hit 14 suits managers buying Liverpool players for the long term, but Gameweeks 13, 15, 16 and 19 are all defensible alternatives.
Haaland is benchable away at Arsenal if the squad is strong enough, but selling him or taking a hit to remove him is not recommended.
Avoid treating young Spurs midfielder Williams-Barnett as a long-term nailed option despite short-term injuries to teammates.

items.title: FPL GW12 TRANSFER PLANS ✅ MY GAMEWEEK 12 TEAM 🎯 RAYA INJURED ⚠️
items.headline: Haaland is benchable against Arsenal, but selling him remains a high-risk play
items.summary:
Erling Haaland's third consecutive blank prompts a serious FPL debate ahead of Manchester City's trip to Arsenal in Gameweek 12. With his effective ownership at 186% for the Fulham match, selling could create a major rank swing if the funds unlock Bruno Fernandes or another premium midfielder. Yet City's schedule improves sharply after Arsenal — Leeds at home, Brentford away, Chelsea at home and Hull at home — and Haaland is still viewed as essential for the Gameweek 16 home fixture against Hull. A sale is therefore a gamble best paired with a clear plan, potentially using Free Hit in Gameweek 16 to restore him; the safer route to Bruno is selling Cole Palmer instead.

Palmer is also under scrutiny after another blank in Chelsea's 4-1 defeat to Leeds, but Forest away and Crystal Palace at home give him two more attractive fixtures before Liverpool and Manchester City offer a natural sell window. Chelsea badly miss João Pedro, while Enzo Fernández is benched and Rayan Cherki is labelled too much of a minutes risk to retain. Leeds assets are rising: Dominic Calvert-Lewin records a goal and assist, while Noah Okafor scores twice and has Coventry, Ipswich and Fulham among his next five. However, the preferred budget-midfield option remains Josh Rudoni, who costs £4.9m, has five attacking returns in five Gameweeks and is on penalties plus some set pieces.

Bournemouth's defence is the standout long-term investment after a ninth straight win in all competitions and another clean sheet. Marcos Senesi and Lloyd Kelly-style defensive returns are represented by Hill and Silva, who both secure DefCon points, while Evanilson extends his scoring run to six consecutive Premier League matches. Bournemouth's fixtures are strong almost until the second Wildcard window, making a defensive double-up viable. Liverpool also offer immediate appeal after a 4.4 xG performance: Wirtz follows a goal and assist with another double-digit haul, and Liverpool attackers are ranked Wirtz then Ekitiké, while Virgil van Dijk and Jarell Quansah are the preferred defensive routes.

The current Gameweek 12 team is set up in a 4-4-2: David Raya; Digne, Van Hecke, Vuskovic and Silva; Mohamed Salah, Bryan Mbeumo, Palmer and Morgan Rogers; Haaland and Jackson. Haaland may be benched against Arsenal, although the alternative, Barry, faces Liverpool. The more urgent issue is Raya's injury. If he is out for a sustained period, James Trafford is the preferred replacement ahead of Alisson, with the switch also freeing funds for a potential Sharda-to-Gibbs-White move in Gameweek 13. If Raya is only absent for two or three weeks, buying Kinsky as cover is attractive because it preserves Raya as a nailed Arsenal asset when fit; if the injury is only one week, even saving the transfer and fielding no goalkeeper is under consideration.
key_points: Haaland is a viable bench option against Arsenal in Gameweek 12, but selling him before City's favourable Gameweek 13-16 run carries major risk.
A Haaland sale works best only if it funds a clear premium upgrade such as Bruno Fernandes and can be reversed with a Gameweek 16 Free Hit plan.
Palmer is retained for Forest away and Crystal Palace at home, with Liverpool and Manchester City likely to form a later sell window.
Rudoni is the preferred budget midfielder at £4.9m after five attacking returns in five Gameweeks, aided by penalties and set pieces.
Okafor is a short-term punt after a brace, with Coventry, Ipswich and Fulham in his next five, but his limited minutes remain a concern.
Bournemouth defenders Hill and Silva are strong long-term buys, with the club's fixture run supporting a defensive double-up.
If Raya's injury is long term, Trafford is the preferred replacement; if it is short term, Kinsky offers a route to keep Raya for later.
Liverpool's Wirtz is an attractive £7.2m midfield option after consecutive double-digit returns, while Van Dijk is the preferred defensive pick.

items.headline: Cole Palmer exit opens Bruno Fernandes and Dominic Calvert-Lewin routes for Gameweek 12
items.summary:
Gameweek 12 shapes as a major transfer point, with managers carrying multiple free transfers and reassessing premium assets after Chelsea and Manchester City disappoint. Cole Palmer is the central dilemma: Chelsea lose heavily to Leeds and look short of cohesion, while Palmer offers little of his previous influence. His fixtures against Nottingham Forest, Crystal Palace and Brentford remain decent, so he is not an automatic sale, but Bruno Fernandes is emerging as the preferred alternative if Manchester United show improvement under Pochettino against Liverpool. Bryan Mbeumo is another route into United’s attacking uplift, although there is a case for waiting until the Gameweek 14 Coventry fixture and using a Free Hit instead.

Nicholas Jackson is not favoured as a captain despite Ipswich away, with Chelsea’s form and the absence of Joao Pedro reducing confidence in their attack. Josh instead plans Castellas to Dominic Calvert-Lewin and captains the Leeds forward against Coventry, backing Leeds’ strong recent performances and Calvert-Lewin’s reliable volume of chances despite his inconsistent finishing. De Cuyper, playing Newcastle at home, is also considered a viable captaincy differential, while Erling Haaland’s trip to Arsenal makes him difficult to trust with the armband. There is even a broader case for selling Haaland temporarily, given City’s flat displays and the depth of cheaper forward options, though his Gameweek 16 home match against Hull is a reason for caution.

Arsenal’s defence is becoming less attractive after a shaky display and a difficult run of Manchester City, Brentford, Tottenham, Bournemouth and Manchester United. Gabriel remains a reasonable hold because of his security, set-piece threat and DefCon potential, but Riccardo Calafiori is viewed as a sellable luxury, particularly if David Raya’s injury absence is confirmed. Neto is rated a significant downgrade in goal, potentially weakening Arsenal’s entire defensive unit. Calafiori can move to a cheaper defender such as Muerovic, Van Hecke, Vuskovic, Silva or James Hill, freeing funds for midfield and forward upgrades.

With four free transfers, the preferred aggressive rebuild is Palmer to Fernandes, Calafiori to Muerovic and Gonzalo to Calvert-Lewin, with a further downgrade of Manzambi if required to fund the moves. The alternative is to avoid immediate United investment, bring in Mbeumo, Jackson and Van Hecke, then Free Hit in Gameweek 14 for triple Manchester United against Coventry alongside Leeds and Bournemouth attackers. Tottenham’s defence remains appealing after a comfortable clean sheet, but Brighton defenders are also in demand; Van Hecke has strong DefCon appeal, while Vuskovic offers a more attacking option. Morgan Gibbs-White is backed to start against Chelsea, whose fragile form makes Nottingham Forest attackers attractive.
key_points: Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the leading Gameweek 12 captaincy pick against Coventry if brought in for Castellas, ahead of Haaland at Arsenal and Jackson at Ipswich.
Cole Palmer is a viable sale despite reasonable fixtures, with Bruno Fernandes the main premium replacement if Manchester United improve against Liverpool.
Riccardo Calafiori is the Arsenal defender most likely to leave squads, while Gabriel remains a hold for his security, DefCon potential and set-piece threat.
David Raya’s potential absence makes Arsenal’s defence less appealing, with Neto seen as a substantial downgrade between the posts.
Josh plans to use one transfer on Castellas to Calvert-Lewin, then aims to preserve transfers for Gameweeks 13-14 and potentially Free Hit in Gameweek 14.
A four-transfer overhaul can pair Palmer to Fernandes and Calafiori to Muerovic with Gonzalo upgraded to Calvert-Lewin, potentially requiring a Manzambi downgrade.
Mbeumo is an alternative to Fernandes for managers who want to delay Manchester United investment until the Gameweek 14 home fixture against Coventry.
Van Hecke, Vuskovic, Muerovic and James Hill are defensive targets as managers move away from Arsenal’s double-up.

items.title: FPL GW11 DEADLINE LIVE! ⏰ Transfers, Bench & Team News 🚨 | Get Your Last Minute FPL Questions In!
items.headline: Vuskovic edges Van Hecke as the Gameweek 11 defensive priority
items.summary:
Gameweek 11 is dominated by unusually difficult bench decisions rather than obvious transfers. Strong squads mean managers are likely to leave returns on the bench, and the key is to accept close calls rather than chase certainty that does not exist. Among the most benchable popular assets are Morgan Gibbs-White, Bryan Mbeumo, Jérémy Doku, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and, due to a risk of reduced minutes, Ezri Konsa. Manzambi is narrowly preferred to Barry, although Manzambi's recent fitness issue and the approaching midweek round make that a marginal call.

The main transfer recommendation is to invest in defence, particularly Brighton. Vuskovic is the preferred new signing over Kaiper and Jan Paul van Hecke for Gameweek 11 because of Brighton's favourable Hull fixture, strong clean-sheet potential and his defensive-contribution upside. Van Hecke remains a good option, while moving Konsa to Vuskovic is more appealing than selling an Arsenal defender: Newcastle's attack is judged to be among the league's weakest on current form, whereas Ipswich still carry enough goal threat to make Arsenal defenders less compelling as transfer targets. Taking a minus four solely to buy Vuskovic is not advised.

Midfield transfers are generally discouraged. Pascal Gross is considered the only midfielder clearly worth actively targeting, with Manzambi the next-best budget option but still a minutes risk after injury. Selling Mbeumo, Cole Palmer or Rayan Cherki simply for another midfielder is seen as a low-upside sideways move; managers are better served upgrading defenders or forwards and using their deep benches. Palmer remains playable because of penalties despite poor recent open-play data, while Haaland is a firm hold even if he blanks again.

Haaland is the leading captain for Gameweek 11, with Nicolas Jackson or Kaiper viable differential alternatives for those avoiding the Manchester City forward. However, the preferred Triple Captain plan is to wait for Haaland's Gameweek 16 fixture against Hull rather than use the chip now. The final squad backs Haaland as captain and consists of Raya; Silva, Calafiori, Kaiper and Vuskovic; Rogers, Palmer, Gross and Barry; Haaland and Jackson, with Sharda first on the bench ahead of Mbeumo and Maherovic. Late Manchester City team news confirms that Cherki and Josko Gvardiol are benched, underlining the rotation concern around both assets.
key_points: Prioritise Konsa to Vuskovic if buying a defender, with Vuskovic favoured over Kaiper and Van Hecke for Brighton's Gameweek 11 trip to Hull.
Do not take a minus four purely to buy Vuskovic, especially with most squads carrying strong bench cover.
Pascal Gross is the standout midfield transfer, while Manzambi is an alternative only if managers can tolerate a minutes risk after injury.
Avoid selling Haaland after another blank; he remains the preferred captain and the better Triple Captain target is Hull in Gameweek 16.
Palmer remains a start because he takes penalties, but his lack of open-play threat makes him a less convincing premium than his price suggests.
Cherki and Gvardiol are benched in Manchester City's Gameweek 11 line-up, reinforcing the rotation risk attached to both.
Bench decisions between Barry, Manzambi, Rogers, Sharda, Konsa and Mbeumo are mostly near-coin flips, so managers should not overreact to inevitable bench points.

items.headline: Haaland remains captain as J Pedro absence drives Jackson transfer calls in Gameweek 11
items.summary:
Erling Haaland remains the preferred captain for Gameweek 11 despite Manchester City’s uneven form and a tougher-than-expected Fulham defence. Nicolas Jackson is the leading alternative and the vice-captain choice, while Alexander Isak and Brighton defender Diper are viable differential captains for managers chasing upside. City’s confirmed team news sees Haaland, Phil Foden and Rayan Cherki start, with Jérémy Doku and Josko Gvardiol benched.

João Pedro is ruled out and is not expected back for Chelsea’s next match either, but the recommendation is not to force a sale if it means sacrificing flexibility. Managers who already own Jackson can bench Pedro and roll a transfer, particularly if they may want to move Cole Palmer to Bruno Fernandes next week. For those without Jackson, Pedro to Jackson is the standout direct move. Evanilson is also a strong longer-term forward option, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Barry are cheaper routes, though neither is as convincing immediately.

Palmer is increasingly difficult to justify, with Chelsea less threatening without Pedro and facing Leeds before a mixed fixture run. However, the advice is largely to hold him for one more week rather than rush into a replacement: Manchester United’s new-manager situation could quickly make Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo or another United asset attractive, and having two free transfers preserves routes to those moves. If selling Palmer now, Florian Wirtz, Morgan Gibbs-White, John McGinn or Antoine Semenyo-style mid-price alternatives are preferred over a forced hit.

Defence is the key transfer market. Brighton’s Jan Paul van Hecke and Vuskovic are recommended buys for their fixtures, clean-sheet potential and DefCon routes to points, with Vuskovic narrowly preferred even for managers already holding Diper. Arsenal’s Riccardo Calafiori and Kieran Konza are expected to start at Newcastle, but William Saliba’s return makes both less secure over the congested Christmas schedule. Selling one Arsenal defender for Van Hecke or Vuskovic is reasonable with multiple free transfers, but selling both is unnecessary. Managers can also wait a week for Muharemovic, whose longer-term rotation with Van Hecke is particularly appealing.

The suggested squad plan is to roll the transfer, bench the injured Pedro and start Haaland as captain with Jackson vice-captain. Raya is the top goalkeeper pick over Verbruggen and Kinsky, while managers still holding Bench Boost are urged to use it now if they have three credible outfield bench players: fixture congestion, suspensions and Arsenal rotation make later opportunities less reliable.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 11, with Jackson the preferred vice-captain and Isak or Diper viable differential alternatives.
João Pedro is ruled out; Pedro to Jackson is a straightforward transfer for managers who do not already own Jackson.
Roll a transfer where possible rather than forcing Palmer out, as Bruno Fernandes or other Manchester United options may become clearer next week.
Vuskovic and Jan Paul van Hecke are the priority defensive buys, with Vuskovic marginally preferred even alongside Diper.
Calafiori and Konza are likely to start against Newcastle, but Saliba’s availability creates growing rotation risk through the festive fixture run.
Do not buy Saliba yet, and avoid selling both Arsenal defenders with only two free transfers.
Raya ranks ahead of Verbruggen and Kinsky for Gameweek 11 goalkeeper selection.
Use Bench Boost this week if the bench is strong, rather than waiting for a more uncertain period of injuries, suspensions and rotation.

items.headline: Jackson replaces João Pedro as Konsa becomes a sell ahead of Arsenal defensive uncertainty
items.summary:
The main move is João Pedro to Nicolas Jackson, with Jackson preferred for Chelsea’s immediate run of Sunderland, Ipswich, Everton, Crystal Palace and Coventry. Jackson carries major ownership risk and offers a credible captaincy option in Gameweek 12 at Ipswich, while João Pedro is viewed as a likely buy-back around Gameweek 16 when Chelsea’s fixtures worsen and his own schedule improves. Selling Evanilson or Barry for Jackson is possible, but Barry’s price, underlying numbers and long-term value make him difficult to discard; João Pedro is the cleaner exit.

Ezri Konsa is the other priority sale, with the move to Luka Vušković planned. William Saliba is fit enough to begin increasing his minutes, leaving Konsa vulnerable even if he starts against Newcastle. Holding Konsa for one more week is acceptable, but the upcoming Manchester City fixture makes the sale inevitable, while Vušković has an attractive immediate fixture and stronger medium-term security. Van Hecke and Djed Spence are also highlighted as excellent defensive buys, with Brighton hosting Ipswich and Spurs facing Hull, but Vušković is the preferred replacement where possible.

Defence is strongly favoured in the current game, with cheap defenders producing a disproportionate number of double-digit hauls and players such as Van Hecke, Vušković, Spence and Gabriel offering strong value. Gabriel is preferred to Calafiori for long-term security, while Raya is valued as safe Arsenal coverage amid uncertainty around Arsenal’s other defensive spots. Managers are encouraged to build depth and prioritise nailed starters before the congested winter schedule, rather than carrying volatile minutes risks such as Rayan Cherki.

Erling Haaland remains the clear captain for Gameweek 11 against Fulham, with Spurs wing-back Spence an unusually strong vice-captain alternative because of his clean-sheet odds and attacking role against Hull. Jackson is the principal non-Haaland captaincy alternative. The advice is to avoid overthinking close bench calls: players such as Barry, Silva, Mbeumo, Sharda and Tavernier are tightly matched, but reliable defensive floors and strong fixtures generally break the ties. Looking ahead, Gameweek 12 is awkward because Haaland visits Arsenal; Jackson at Ipswich, Mbeumo against Brentford and Dominic Calvert-Lewin are among the captaincy routes to consider.
key_points: Transfer João Pedro to Nicolas Jackson for Chelsea’s favourable Gameweeks 11-15, with a potential Jackson-to-João Pedro reversal around Gameweek 16.
Sell Ezri Konsa for Luka Vušković now or next week, as Saliba’s return threatens Konsa’s minutes and Arsenal face Manchester City in Gameweek 12.
Van Hecke, Vušković and Spence are the standout defensive buys this week, led by Brighton’s home fixture against Ipswich and Spurs’ trip to Hull.
Captain Haaland against Fulham; Spence is an elite vice-captain option, while Jackson is the strongest alternative captain.
Prioritise nailed players and a playable bench for the dense winter calendar, making Cherki a transfer-out candidate because of his erratic minutes.
Gabriel is a meaningful upgrade on Calafiori for safer Arsenal coverage, while Raya remains the most secure Arsenal defensive pick.
Avoid unnecessary hits for defenders unless the replacement is a major upgrade over a player who must otherwise start.
Gameweek 12 may justify looking beyond Haaland at Arsenal, with Jackson at Ipswich and Mbeumo at Brentford among the leading captaincy options.

items.title: FPL Gameweek 11 Deadline Stream 🚀 Konsa 🆚 DCL 🆚 Mbeumo 🤔
items.headline: Haaland Captained as Calvert-Lewin Gets the Nod Over Konsa and Mbeumo
items.summary:
Erling Haaland remains the clear captaincy choice for Gameweek 11 at home to Fulham. Nicolas Jackson, Cole Palmer and Ekitike offer viable differential routes, but Haaland’s superior open-play goal threat and penalty duties make him the preferred option despite the temptation to chase Jackson’s recent form. A Triple Captain on Haaland is acceptable this week, although the fixture against Hull in Gameweek 16 is viewed as an even stronger potential chip opportunity.

The final squad call is to start Dominic Calvert-Lewin ahead of Arsenal defender Konsa and Bryan Mbeumo. It is an extremely close benching decision: Konsa has Arsenal’s defensive strength and Newcastle’s poor form in his favour, while Mbeumo offers strong open-play numbers and a possible new-manager bounce for Manchester United. Calvert-Lewin ultimately gets the place because he is nailed for close to 90 minutes, leads the line and takes penalties, even though Chelsea away is not an ideal fixture and his away-goal record is poor. Konsa is left as second substitute.

The only transfer is Lewis Hall to Vuskovic, adding a strong long-term defensive asset. Van Hecke is marginally preferred for the immediate Gameweek 11 fixture, while Vuskovic is rated better over the following two gameweeks and as the safer longer-term buy. Managers intending to own both are advised to buy Van Hecke first; those choosing only one should favour Vuskovic. Arsenal defenders are still good short-term picks, but Konsa is expected to become a sell soon as William Saliba returns, with the view that Konsa will not retain a regular starting role or become a reliable right-back option.

Looking ahead, Bruno Fernandes is a major Gameweek 12 consideration, particularly as a differential captain against Chelsea. The preferred route is either Palmer to Bruno, potentially funded by a defensive downgrade, or using a Free Hit in Gameweek 14 to target Bruno against Coventry instead. Manchester United’s result at Liverpool should not dictate the decision too heavily: Bruno remains attractive because he is on penalties, plays almost every minute and has a favourable fixture run from Gameweeks 12 to 15. Managers with strong benches are urged to use Bench Boost early rather than waiting for a theoretical better week, as midweek matches, injuries, suspensions and rotation are likely to make the chip harder to deploy.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Fulham in Gameweek 11; Jackson and Palmer are alternatives but rank below him.
Start Calvert-Lewin over Konsa and Mbeumo because he is a nailed penalty taker, despite Chelsea away.
Transfer Lewis Hall to Vuskovic for a stronger long-term defensive option.
Buy Van Hecke before Vuskovic only if planning to own both soon; otherwise Vuskovic is the preferred longer-term pick.
Konsa is expected to start in Gameweeks 11 and 12 but is not considered a long-term Arsenal asset once Saliba is fully reintegrated.
Consider Palmer to Bruno Fernandes in Gameweek 12, but preserve the option of a Gameweek 14 Free Hit if possible.
Use Bench Boost promptly when the bench contains viable starters rather than waiting for a perfect double or future setup.
Avoid buying four-yellow-card players such as Silva, Tavares or Gross solely for a short-term upgrade if a suspension could disrupt immediate plans.

items.headline: Joao Pedro absence pushes Palmer sale into focus as Haaland remains Gameweek 11 captain
items.summary:
William Saliba is ready to return for Arsenal after building fitness in behind-closed-doors friendlies, making Ezri Konsa and Riccardo Calafiori less secure over a punishing run of Manchester City, Brentford, Spurs, Real Madrid and Bournemouth. Both are still expected to start at Newcastle in Gameweek 11, so an immediate sale is not essential, but neither is a buy. Gabriel remains the secure Arsenal defensive route, while Raya offers the set-and-forget goalkeeper option. Brighton defenders such as De Kuijper, Vuskovic and Van Hecke are attractive alternatives, particularly with Ipswich next.

Joao Pedro is ruled out of Chelsea's home match against Leeds and may not return until December, a blow both to his own ownership and to Cole Palmer's appeal. Chelsea have scored in only one league match without Joao Pedro this season, so Palmer's premium price looks increasingly difficult to justify even though he remains a start this week. Morgan Rogers is still a viable budget midfielder on form, but Joao Pedro is likely to be sold in Gameweek 12 rather than forced out now if there is no compelling forward replacement. Nicolas Jackson is the priority forward target behind Erling Haaland, with Alexander Isak a strong but expensive alternative and Evanilson, Barry and Dominic Calvert-Lewin cheaper routes.

Manchester United are a wait-and-see under Mauricio Pochettino, beginning with Liverpool away. Reports of a possible back-five shape from training only reinforce the uncertainty around roles, with Bruno Fernandes, Matheus Cunha and Joshua Zirkzee potentially benefiting more than wing-back options such as Brandon Williams. There is no case to buy a United player before Gameweek 11; assess their Liverpool, European and Brentford matches before targeting the improved fixtures from Gameweek 12 onwards.

Haaland is the clear captain at home to Fulham despite consecutive league blanks, with Jackson the leading vice-captain against Sunderland and Isak a credible differential at home to Manchester United. Wildcarding in Gameweek 11 is not advised because of uncertainty over United assets and the difficult choice between Bruno, Isak and Gabriel alongside Haaland. A bench boost is worth using now for managers already set up, while the current squad plan is to roll a transfer, start Joao Pedro only if necessary from the bench, and use two moves in Gameweek 12 to restructure around his absence and potentially move Palmer.
key_points: Saliba's return reduces Konsa and Calafiori's long-term security, although both are still expected to start at Newcastle in Gameweek 11.
Gabriel and Raya are Arsenal's safest defensive picks; De Kuijper, Vuskovic and Van Hecke are strong alternatives for Brighton's favourable fixtures.
Joao Pedro is out against Leeds and may miss Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace too, making a Gameweek 12 sale likely.
Palmer remains playable in Gameweek 11 but becomes a leading sell candidate because Chelsea are markedly weaker without Joao Pedro.
Do not buy Manchester United players before Liverpool away; wait for clarity on Pochettino's system and preferred attackers.
Captain Haaland against Fulham, with Jackson against Sunderland the preferred vice-captain and Isak a differential option.
Avoid a Gameweek 11 wildcard unless essential; use a well-prepared bench boost now rather than saving it without a clear future plan.
Rolling a transfer is preferable to selling Joao Pedro for an unconvincing replacement and creating a difficult benching decision.

items.title: FPL GW11 Team Selection: Goodbye Konsa, Hello Free Hit! 💥 | Transfers & Captain
items.headline: Haaland is the clear Gameweek 11 captain as Konaté replacement becomes priority
items.summary:
Gameweek 11 is set up as a defence-heavy week, with Erling Haaland the standout captain at home to Fulham. Manchester City carry the highest projected goal total of the round and Haaland remains the focal point of their attack despite recent Premier League blanks. Nicolas Jackson, at home to Sunderland, is vice-captain, while Everton forward Barry keeps his place because he dominates Everton’s chance volume and arrives in strong finishing form.

The preferred starting defence is a four-man unit of Riccardo Calafiori, Ezri Konsa, Micky van de Ven and Thiago Silva, alongside Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya. Arsenal’s trip to Newcastle is considered better than it looks: Newcastle’s non-penalty xG has been among the weakest in the league, making Arsenal’s defensive triple-up appealing. Brighton have the best clean-sheet odds against Hull, strengthening the case for Van de Ven, while Silva remains a high-upside Bournemouth defender because of strong team defensive numbers, defensive-contribution potential and bonus appeal against Nottingham Forest.

The likely transfer is Konsa to Luka Vuskovic. William Saliba is nearing a return after friendly and Under-21 minutes, creating a growing risk that Konsa loses starts, minutes or defensive-contribution opportunities. Konsa may still start against Newcastle and could reach 60 minutes, but his long-term security is deteriorating. Vuskovic offers better immediate clean-sheet odds against Hull, stronger historical threat for defensive contributions and set-piece returns, and an appealing run in eight of the next nine gameweeks. The move also potentially catches a price rise.

Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers start against Leeds despite uninspiring recent underlying numbers, largely because midfield alternatives are unconvincing. Pascal Gross returns to the XI for Hull after being benched for 10 points in Gameweek 10; the earlier benching is accepted as an understandable differential call, but Gross’s next two fixtures are too good to ignore. Sharda is first substitute rather than a starter against Everton, with Callum Wilson now more likely than Sharda to take penalties if Thiago is unavailable. Bryan Mbeumo is retained despite Liverpool away, as his underlying data remains elite and Manchester United’s new-manager effect may help; Gameweek 16 at Arsenal is viewed as a more logical sale point.

Looking ahead, a Gameweek 13 Free Hit is planned to avoid Brighton versus Bournemouth and target players unavailable through normal transfers, notably Liverpool and Chelsea assets in a midweek round. Before that, the intended Gameweek 12 double move is Palmer and Barry out for Manzambi and Dominic Calvert-Lewin, subject to Manzambi’s fitness. That targets favourable fixtures before using the Free Hit to field a radically different side, potentially including double Liverpool defence, Chelsea attackers, Spurs defenders and Crystal Palace’s Daniel Muñoz.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Fulham in Gameweek 11, with Jackson at home to Sunderland as vice-captain.
Make Konsa to Vuskovic the priority transfer because Saliba’s return increasingly threatens Konsa’s minutes and upside.
Start Raya, Calafiori and Konsa against a low-output Newcastle attack, while Vuskovic is favoured for Brighton’s home match with Hull.
Gross starts against Hull after his Gameweek 10 bench haul, with Brighton’s upcoming fixtures making him too strong to bench again.
Sharda stays first on the bench against Everton, as Callum Wilson is now considered the likelier penalty taker if Thiago misses out.
Hold Mbeumo despite Liverpool away: his recent shot and xG numbers remain strong, with a possible exit pencilled in for Gameweek 16 at Arsenal.
Plan Palmer and Barry to Manzambi and Calvert-Lewin in Gameweek 12, then deploy the Free Hit in Gameweek 13 to attack Liverpool, Chelsea, Spurs and Crystal Palace fixtures.

items.title: JOÃO PEDRO LATEST ⚠️ | FPL GW11 INJURY + TEAM NEWS 🚨|  FPL Tips 2026/27
items.headline: Joao Pedro and Bukayo Saka headline Gameweek 11 injury absences
items.summary:
Fantasy Premier League managers face a busy Gameweek 11 team-news round, with Chelsea’s Joao Pedro the most important confirmed absentee. The forward has not returned to team training and is ruled out, while Bukayo Saka is expected to miss around another four weeks after Arsenal confirm he is only halfway through an eight-week rehabilitation period. Manchester City’s Erling Haaland has no reported fitness concern for Fulham, making him available for the early Saturday captaincy conversation despite the perceived risk of a 12:30pm kick-off.

Chelsea otherwise receive encouraging updates: Moises Caicedo is fit after illness concerns, Enzo Fernandez is available, and Aaron Anselmino is back in the squad, but Reece James, Max Lavia and Jamie Gittens remain unavailable or short of match fitness. Arsenal’s William Saliba has returned to action in youth and behind-closed-doors games, yet is still being managed carefully; Cristhian Mosquera is therefore likely to retain his place for now. Newcastle have few issues beyond Joelinton’s hamstring problem, while Liverpool expect Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch, Jeremie Frimpong and Dominik Szoboszlai to be available.

There are several defensive and midfield concerns elsewhere. Aston Villa’s Matty Cash must follow concussion protocol after a head injury with Poland and is expected back in Gameweek 12, while Boubacar Kamara, Amadou Onana and Roger are still out. Sunderland lose Granit Xhaka to a potentially significant calf injury and Brian Brobbey to a thigh problem, although Omar Alderete returns from suspension. Nottingham Forest must assess Callum Hudson-Odoi, Nicolas Dominguez, Nicolas Williams and Alexander Schlager, while Brentford are particularly depleted: Nathan Collins and Aaron Hickey are sidelined for weeks and Igor Thiago begins a three-match suspension.

Managers considering attacking replacements should note that Bournemouth’s Justin Kluivert is ready to start and may increasingly threaten Eli Junior Kroupi’s role, while Alex Scott is being built up for starts over the next three matches. Tottenham have Lucas Bergvall, Destiny Udogie and James Maddison available again, but Mathys Tel is out for roughly three weeks. Everton welcome Jack Grealish back into the senior group and he is expected to be involved against Brentford. Fulham’s Josh King is fit despite recent groin pain, but Emile Smith Rowe misses out with a hip issue.
key_points: Erling Haaland has no reported fitness concern for Manchester City’s home match against Fulham and remains available for Gameweek 11 captaincy.
Joao Pedro is ruled out for Chelsea after failing to return to full training, making him a pressing transfer concern for his owners.
Bukayo Saka is expected to miss roughly another month, with Arsenal targeting a return around mid-December.
Brentford lose Nathan Collins and Aaron Hickey for weeks, while Igor Thiago starts a three-match ban after a failed appeal.
Matty Cash is unavailable for Aston Villa due to concussion protocol and is expected to return in Gameweek 12.
Granit Xhaka has a calf injury that is likely to keep him out for an extended spell, while Sunderland striker Brian Brobbey also misses Aston Villa with a thigh issue.
Justin Kluivert is fit to start for Bournemouth, increasing the threat to Eli Junior Kroupi’s minutes, while Alex Scott is being gradually restored.
Liverpool expect Van Dijk, Gravenberch, Frimpong and Szoboszlai to be fit, with Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni back in partial training but not yet ready to play.

items.title: 🚨 João Pedro is OUT 🚨 FPL GW11 Final Thoughts 🤔
items.headline: Haaland is the locked captain as Konsa minutes become a growing concern in Gameweek 11
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the clear captain for Gameweek 11 at home to Fulham, while the main selection issue is whether to risk Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa at Newcastle. William Saliba is fit again after two behind-closed-doors matches and is expected to reclaim substantial minutes for Arsenal soon. Konsa may still start this week, but he is no longer secure enough to win close calls: Calafiori is preferred if choosing between the two Arsenal defenders, while reliable starters such as Iliman Ndiaye and Dominic Calvert-Lewin also rank ahead of Konsa in bench decisions.

João Pedro is ruled out for Chelsea in Gameweek 11 and has not returned to team training, making him a sell for most managers, particularly those without Nicolas Jackson. Jackson is viewed as a strong one-transfer replacement with a good five-week fixture run, while Hugo Ekitiké is also attractive if managers can afford him. Calvert-Lewin can be retained for now, with appealing home fixtures in Gameweeks 12 and 14. Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers remain starts against Leeds despite Chelsea looking less effective without João Pedro; his absence is a concern, but not sufficient reason alone to make a rushed sale before this fixture.

Among defenders, Jan Paul van Hecke offers the safest guaranteed minutes, Luka Vuskovic combines strong security with favourable medium-term fixtures, and Brighton’s Maxim De Cuyper has the highest upside if he keeps his place. De Cuyper is a viable buy despite the possible future threat from Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh, but buyers must accept that he may need selling again if his minutes decline. Konsa is the bigger longer-term sell than Calafiori because Saliba is expected to become Arsenal’s first-choice right-sided centre-back, whereas Calafiori remains first choice at left-back even if he is occasionally rested in congested periods.

Milos Kerkez is favoured over Bournemouth’s Marcos Senesi for new purchases despite Senesi’s superior defensive-contribution potential. Senesi is already on four yellow cards, creating a suspension risk that is manageable only for squads with strong cover. Kerkez has excellent Liverpool fixtures ahead, fewer disciplinary concerns and enough defensive-contribution potential to be a dependable alternative. The preferred personal Gameweek 11 setup is a 4-3-3, with Raya and Calafiori joining De Cuyper, Vuskovic and Van Hecke in defence; Palmer, Rogers and Pascal Gross in midfield; and Calvert-Lewin, Jackson and captain Haaland up front. Bryan Mbeumo is edged out by Calvert-Lewin, mainly because Calvert-Lewin is nailed for penalties and Chelsea’s defence has been vulnerable.

With three free transfers available, the recommendation is still to roll rather than force a marginal defensive move. A Gameweek 13 midweek round and the Christmas schedule should create more urgent injuries, rotation issues and opportunities, making transfer flexibility especially valuable. Managers considering a Bench Boost can likely use it with Bobby Thomas if he returns to Coventry’s starting side after training, but should delay or use a transfer if they are unconvinced he starts.
key_points: Captain Haaland at home to Fulham in Gameweek 11; the armband is described as locked.
Sell João Pedro in most squads after confirmation that he is out for Gameweek 11 and not yet training with Chelsea.
Start Palmer and Rogers against Leeds, but reassess Palmer before Gameweek 12 if João Pedro’s absence continues to hurt Chelsea’s attack.
Bench Konsa in close calls despite a likely start at Newcastle, as Saliba’s return creates a significant medium-term minutes risk.
Van Hecke is the safest defensive purchase, Vuskovic is the secure longer-term option, and De Cuyper has the greatest upside if his starts continue.
Prefer Kerkez to buying Senesi for Liverpool’s fixture run because Senesi is one yellow card from suspension.
Calvert-Lewin is preferred to Mbeumo for the final attacking spot, with penalties and Chelsea’s defensive weakness breaking a close call.
Avoid forcing a transfer and preserve flexibility for the Gameweek 13 midweek round and Christmas congestion.

items.title: HAALAND CAPTAIN! 🧢 | Josh's GW11 FPL Team Selection
items.headline: Haaland leads Gameweek 11 front line as Gibbs-White challenges Castulas for final start
items.summary:
Kinsky starts in goal for the home meeting with Ipswich after recording two clean sheets in his last three appearances. The defence is built around Arsenal’s trip to Newcastle, with Gabriel and Calafiori both starting despite the away fixture. Van de Ven completes a Tottenham defensive double-up against Ipswich, while Digne keeps his place because he continues to operate high on the left wing and offers attacking upside.

The midfield is restricted to Pascal Groß, Tavernier and Morgan Rogers. All three are viewed as relatively template selections, but that is accepted because they provide dependable routes to points and have favourable enough Gameweek 11 prospects. The selection prioritises reliable starters over forcing a more aggressive differential into the XI.

Up front, Castulas is currently selected alongside Erling Haaland, who has a home fixture against Fulham, and Nicolas Jackson, who faces Sunderland at home. Haaland and Jackson are straightforward starts because of their fixtures, leaving Castulas as the vulnerable forward slot.

The main dilemma is whether to retain Castulas or bring Morgan Gibbs-White off the bench. Gibbs-White returns an attacking haul last week and Nottingham Forest look in strong form, while Castulas has recently struggled for FPL returns. Leno, Kevin Schade and Lewis Hall complete the bench, with Gibbs-White the leading substitute option if recent form is given greater weight than the existing forward selection.
key_points: Kinsky starts at home to Ipswich after two clean sheets in his last three matches.
Gabriel and Calafiori start away at Newcastle, maintaining Arsenal defensive coverage despite the difficult fixture.
Van de Ven joins the Spurs double-up for Ipswich at home, while Digne is backed for his advanced left-sided role.
Pascal Groß, Tavernier and Morgan Rogers form the three-man midfield and are selected as dependable, template options.
Haaland is a clear starter at home to Fulham, with Nicolas Jackson also starting at home to Sunderland.
The key selection call is Castulas versus Gibbs-White: Castulas is currently in the XI, but Gibbs-White's recent return and Forest’s form make him a strong alternative.
Leno, Kevin Schade and Lewis Hall are also on the bench.

items.title: FPL GW11 EXPERTS TEAM 🚀 430x Top 10k! 🚨
items.headline: Haaland dominates Gameweek 11 captaincy as experts pivot from Konsa to Vaskovich
items.summary:
Gameweek 11 is a quiet week for the leading FPL managers, with 52% planning to roll a transfer and 34% making one move. The dominant transfer trend is a defensive reshuffle: Vaskovich and Van Hecke are the two clear priority buys, while Hall and Konsa are the main sales. Vaskovich has returned 46 points over the past six gameweeks, level with Konsa and second only to Jackson over that period, while Van Hecke has 39. Their appealing immediate fixtures, including Hull away and Ipswich at home, make them attractive replacements for Konsa even if he is fit to start.

Konsa owners are also reacting to Arsenal’s difficult next two fixtures, away at Newcastle and home to Manchester City, plus uncertainty over his minutes. Hall faces Arsenal, Brighton away and Manchester United next, prompting widespread sales. Arsenal still top the clean-sheet projections through to the new year, ahead of Manchester City, Liverpool, Brighton, Bournemouth and Spurs, so Gabriel remains a premium target despite being awkward to buy. Xhaka and Van Dijk are flagged as lower-owned defensive alternatives, while cheaper options such as Vaskovich, Silva, Hill, Van Hecke and Nald offer routes into favourable fixture runs.

Erling Haaland is the overwhelming captaincy selection for Fulham away, backed by 98% of the experts. De Bruyne receives the other 2% and offers a major differential given his league-leading 75 points and potential left-wing role if Mendy misses out, but Haaland remains the safest choice. Fulham’s defensive numbers have improved markedly, conceding just 6.4 xG over the past six matches, so their recent resilience is worth noting, although it is not considered enough to overturn Haaland’s captaincy appeal. Jackson is the main alternative from the usual premium options.

The busy run of 10 gameweeks in 45 days increases the value of squad depth and transfer flexibility. Sean Regan activates Bench Boost with Raya, Vaskovich, Silva, Caligiuri, Palmer, Rogers, Ryan, Gross, Haaland, Jackson and Evan Nelson, supported by Kinski, Man Zambi, Van Hecke and Thomas on the bench. He views the immediate post-international-break week as an imperfect but sensible chance to use the chip before Christmas rotation, injuries and suspensions make a later Bench Boost harder to plan. Mbeumo and Thomas are fitness concerns; McGinn is the likely Mbeumo replacement, while Thomas could become Van Hecke.

Managers are also beginning to plan for fixture turns beyond Gameweek 11. Building free transfers is preferred amid uncertainty over Arsenal defenders and possible Manchester United attacking targets, with Bruno Fernandes, Bowen and Cunha on the longer-term watchlist. A potential Free Hit in Gameweek 14 is being considered by some, while strong benches are increasingly important through the festive schedule.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Fulham, with 98% of experts backing him; De Bruyne is the only meaningful differential captain choice.
Vaskovich and Van Hecke are the leading Gameweek 11 transfer targets, helped by strong recent returns and favourable fixtures.
Sell Hall if possible before fixtures against Arsenal, Brighton and Manchester United, while Konsa is widely moved on because of tougher games and potential minutes concerns.
Arsenal lead clean-sheet projections until the new year, making Gabriel an appealing but expensive defensive upgrade.
Roll a transfer where possible: 52% of leading managers plan to save their move amid injury and rotation uncertainty.
Bench Boost is viable for managers with a strong 15, but Mbeumo and Thomas need late fitness checks before committing.
Monitor Bruno Fernandes ahead of Manchester United’s Gameweek 14-15 fixtures, when Palmer faces Liverpool and Manchester City.
